author: Elastic
rule.description:
Detects git clone, git push, or ZIP download authenticated with a classic PAT, fine-grained PAT, or OAuth access token
from an autonomous system (ASN) not previously seen for that user in the last 7 days. The source IP is resolved to its
ASN at query time, so address churn inside the same ISP or cloud provider does not produce new alerts. A token used
from an unfamiliar ASN can indicate credential theft or use from an unauthorized location.
false_positives:
CI, laptops, or travel networks using the same PAT or OAuth token from a new egress IP. Confirm the token owner and
    whether the repositories are expected.
rule.name: GitHub Token Clone Push or ZIP from Unusual ASN
rule.note:
## Triage and analysis

### Investigating GitHub Token Clone Push or ZIP from Unusual ASN

First-seen `user.name` + ASN on `git.clone`, `git.push`, or `repo.download_zip` over a 7-day look-back, using classic PATs, fine-grained PATs, or OAuth tokens. The IP is resolved to its ASN at query time (`IP_LOCATION` / GeoLite2-ASN), so this keys on the source network rather than the raw IP — address churn inside one ISP or cloud provider does not re-alert. Sibling production rule `GitHub Activity on a Private Repository from an Unusual ASN` applies the same ASN approach to clone/push on private repos.

### Possible investigation steps

- Identify `user.name`, the new ASN (`Esql.source_as_number` / `Esql.source_as_organization_name`), `github.programmatic_access_type`, the token (`Esql_priv.token_id_values`), and the repositories (`Esql.repo_values`).
- Review the IPs and countries observed for the ASN (`Esql.source_ip_values`, `Esql.country_values`) and whether they match the token owner's known locations.
- Correlate with `personal_access_token.access_granted` and collaborator adds from the same ASN or token.

### False positive analysis

- Developers travelling or switching between home, mobile, and corporate networks appear from a new ASN the first time each is used.
- Shared automation tokens or CI appear once per cloud provider ASN; add exceptions for known automation identities if the volume is high.

### Response and remediation

- Revoke the token if the ASN is not the owner's. Review clones and ZIP downloads in the same window.
rule.query:
FROM logs-github.audit-*
| WHERE event.dataset == "github.audit"
  AND event.action IN ("git.clone", "git.push", "repo.download_zip")
  AND github.programmatic_access_type IN ("OAuth access token", "Fine-grained personal access token", "Personal access token")
  AND user.name IS NOT NULL AND github.actor_ip IS NOT NULL
| IP_LOCATION asn = github.actor_ip WITH { "database_file": "GeoLite2-ASN.mmdb", "properties": ["asn", "organization_name"] }
| IP_LOCATION geo = github.actor_ip WITH { "properties": ["country_iso_code"] }
| WHERE asn.asn IS NOT NULL
| STATS Esql.event_count = COUNT(*),
        Esql.first_seen = MIN(@timestamp),
        Esql.last_seen = MAX(@timestamp),
        Esql.source_ip_values = VALUES(github.actor_ip),
        Esql.country_values = VALUES(geo.country_iso_code),
        Esql.repo_values = VALUES(github.repo),
        Esql.event_action_values = VALUES(event.action),
        Esql.programmatic_access_type_values = VALUES(github.programmatic_access_type),
        Esql.user_agent_values = VALUES(github.user_agent),
        Esql_priv.token_id_values = VALUES(github.token_id),
        Esql_priv.hashed_token_values = VALUES(github.hashed_token)
  BY user.name, asn.asn, asn.organization_name
// The 7-day history is the rule look-back (from = now-10085m). A group is new when its first event
// falls inside the current interval; the 10m bound allows for the 5m interval plus scheduling drift.
// Novelty is keyed on user + ASN only, so a new IP inside an already-seen ASN does not re-alert.
| WHERE DATE_DIFF("minute", Esql.first_seen, NOW()) <= 10
| EVAL Esql.source_as_number = asn.asn,
       Esql.source_as_organization_name = asn.organization_name
| KEEP user.name, Esql.*, Esql_priv.*
